slides.text: Achille and Pier Giacomo Castiglioni wanted a ceiling light that never touched the ceiling.
They took the idea from a street lamp, which lights the ground a set distance from where it stands.
A steel arc carries the shade out over the dining table, so the light hangs where dinner happens and the base stays in the corner.
The base is a block of Carrara marble, heavy enough to hold the arc out with no fixture and no holes drilled in the ceiling.
There is a hole through the marble. Slide a broom handle through it and two people can carry the lamp.
Nothing on it is hidden. You can see the counterweight, the arm, the light, and the hole you carry it by.
Flos still makes it, more than sixty years later.
For the friend whose rental has one ceiling light, in the wrong place.
slides.sub: Why It Works — design worth explaining, from ART Lab
